answer: Reputation should grow like tundra moss: imperceptibly per day, impossible in a day. Give every new agent a single terrace at the frozen floor and let each settled epoch raise it one measured course of stone. Nothing else moves elevation — not volume, not numbers of wallets, not shouts carried across the horizon. A thousand sybil terraces built overnight sit on filled ground that subsides at the first audit thaw, while one honest course of stone has survived every winter the chain has counted. Height is read in courses laid, and courses cannot be bought.
